finds.title: Public Law 107-296, Homeland Security Act of 2002
finds.author: United States Congress
finds.evidence_quote: There is established a Department of Homeland Security, as an executive department of the United States within the meaning of title 5, United States Code.
finds.line: Congress created the Department of Homeland Security as an executive department, giving it the mission that now covers the border and immigration workforce.
finds.about: This is the public law that set up the Department of Homeland Security. It was approved on November 25, 2002. Title I sets up the department and states its primary mission, which begins with preventing terrorist attacks within the United States.
finds.because: The new department brought the border and immigration agencies together under one workforce, the same workforce whose names were later published.

finds.title: Warner, Kaine Push ICE to Require Agents Identify Themselves, Limit Use of Masks and Face Coverings During Enforcement Operations
finds.author: Sen. Mark R. Warner and Sen. Tim Kaine
finds.source: Office of Sen. Mark R. Warner (warner.senate.gov)
finds.evidence_quote: Across the country and in Virginia, masked ICE officers and agents without clearly visible identification as law enforcement have been arresting individuals on the streets and in sensitive locations, such as courthouses.
finds.line: Senators Warner and Kaine wrote to ICE and DHS asking for their rules on face coverings and on revealing officer identities during immigration arrests.
finds.about: Two senators released this letter and press statement in May 2025. They said masked ICE officers without clear identification were making arrests on streets and at courthouses. They asked DHS and ICE for policies, guidance and training materials on masks and officer identity.
finds.ties_to: officials who mask up and wear plain clothes in American cities
finds.because: The letter put the masking question on the record in Congress, setting up the fight over whether agents' identities should be hidden or public.

finds.title: Cybersecurity Incidents
finds.author: U.S. Office of Personnel Management
finds.evidence_quote: In 2015, OPM announced two separate but related cybersecurity incidents that have impacted the data of Federal government employees, contractors, and others
finds.line: In 2015, OPM announced two separate but related cybersecurity incidents that affected the data of federal government employees, contractors, and others.
finds.about: OPM, the federal personnel agency, announced the incidents in 2015. There were two of them, and they were separate but related. They affected the data of federal employees, contractors, and other people.
finds.ties_to: records of more than 41,000 DHS employees taken by hackers
finds.relation: earlier instance of the same action
finds.because: The 2015 breach showed that stolen federal workforce data could reach millions of people, which framed later worries about who holds staff records and how well they are guarded.

finds.title: Congress Passes the Daniel Anderl Judicial Security and Privacy Act
finds.author: Administrative Office of the U.S. Courts
finds.evidence_quote: It also will allow federal judges to redact personal information displayed on federal government internet sites and prevent publication of personal information by other businesses and individuals where there is no legitimate news media or other public interest.
finds.line: Congress passed the Daniel Anderl Act, letting federal judges redact personal details on government websites and limiting publication of that information by others.
finds.about: Congress passed the act on December 16, 2022. It lets federal judges redact personal information shown on federal government internet sites. It also bars businesses and individuals from publishing that information where no legitimate news media or other public interest exists.
finds.ties_to: laws protecting law enforcement personal information
finds.because: This law gave Congress a working model for limiting publication of officials' personal details, and later bills on officers' names borrowed the same idea.

finds.title: New York Times Co. v. Sullivan, 376 U.S. 254 (1964)
finds.author: Justice William J. Brennan, Jr., for the Supreme Court of the United States
finds.source: Justia, U.S. Supreme Court Center (opinion text)
finds.evidence_quote: Respondent, an elected official in Montgomery, Alabama, brought suit in a state court alleging that he had been libeled by an advertisement in corporate petitioner's
finds.line: In New York Times Co. v. Sullivan, the Court heard a libel suit that an elected Alabama official brought over a newspaper advertisement.
finds.about: The case began when an elected official in Montgomery, Alabama, sued in a state court. He said an advertisement had libeled him. The advertisement was published by the corporate petitioner, the New York Times Co. The Court issued its decision in March 1964.
finds.ties_to: attack ad calling Acton a liar
finds.because: It set the rule for when a public figure can sue over false statements in political speech, the legal setting any later attack ad about a candidate is judged in.

finds.title: Susan B. Anthony List v. Driehaus
finds.author: Justice Clarence Thomas, for a unanimous Supreme Court of the United States
finds.source: Legal Information Institute, Cornell Law School (Supreme Court opinion text)
finds.evidence_quote: Petitioners in this case seek to challenge an Ohio statute that prohibits certain "false statements" during the course of a political campaign.
finds.line: In Susan B. Anthony List v. Driehaus, petitioners sought to challenge an Ohio law that bars certain false statements during political campaigns.
finds.about: The petitioners in this case wanted to challenge an Ohio statute. The law prohibits certain "false statements" made during the course of a political campaign. The Court issued its decision in June 2014.
finds.ties_to: Ohio governor's race, ad calling Acton a liar
finds.because: It put Ohio's rules on false campaign statements, and the Elections Commission complaint process, before the nation's highest court twelve years before the 2026 governor's race.

finds.title: Introducing ChatGPT
finds.author: OpenAI
finds.evidence_quote: ChatGPT and GPT‑3.5 were trained on an Azure AI supercomputing infrastructure.
finds.line: OpenAI introduced ChatGPT, a conversational model that it said was trained on an Azure AI supercomputing infrastructure.
finds.about: This is OpenAI's own launch post for ChatGPT, published in November 2022. It describes how the model was trained with human feedback and lists its limits. It also says the model was trained on Microsoft's Azure cloud hardware.
finds.ties_to: how much Big Tech is spending on artificial intelligence
finds.because: The public release of ChatGPT set off the race among large technology firms to fund AI computing capacity.

finds.title: Microsoft and OpenAI extend partnership
finds.author: Microsoft Corporate Blogs
finds.evidence_quote: Today, we are announcing the third phase of our long-term partnership with OpenAI through a multiyear, multibillion dollar investment to accelerate AI breakthroughs to ensure these benefits are broadly shared with the world.
finds.line: Microsoft announced the third phase of its long-term partnership with OpenAI, backed by a multiyear, multibillion dollar investment meant to speed up AI breakthroughs.
finds.about: The announcement came on January 23, 2023, when Microsoft said it was extending its partnership with OpenAI. The company described a multiyear, multibillion dollar investment. Its stated goal was to accelerate AI breakthroughs and make sure the benefits are broadly shared with the world.
finds.ties_to: Big Tech is spending on artificial intelligence
finds.relation: earlier instance of the same action
finds.because: A major platform company put a public, large-scale bet on AI soon after ChatGPT, pushing rivals such as Google to match it.

finds.title: NVIDIA Announces Financial Results for First Quarter Fiscal 2024
finds.author: NVIDIA Corporation
finds.source: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Form 8-K, EDGAR)
finds.evidence_quote: We are significantly increasing our supply to meet surging demand for them," he said.
finds.line: NVIDIA reported its first quarter fiscal 2024 results and said it was significantly increasing its supply to meet surging demand for its products.
finds.about: NVIDIA released these results on May 24, 2023, for the first quarter of fiscal 2024. In a statement, an executive said the company was significantly increasing its supply. He described the reason as surging demand for the company's offerings.
finds.ties_to: how much Big Tech is spending on artificial intelligence
finds.because: The chip maker's results showed that the AI spending of cloud and internet firms was turning into real revenue for suppliers.

finds.title: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2025 Results
finds.author: Alphabet Inc.
finds.source: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1, EDGAR)
finds.evidence_quote: With the growth across our business and demand from Cloud customers, we now expect 2025 capital expenditures to be in a range of $91 billion to $93 billion.
finds.line: Alphabet announced its third quarter 2025 results and raised its outlook, now expecting 2025 capital expenditures in a range of $91 billion to $93 billion.
finds.about: Alphabet shared these results on October 29, 2025. The company pointed to growth across its business and demand from Cloud customers. Because of this, it said it now expected 2025 capital expenditures to fall in a range of $91 billion to $93 billion.
finds.ties_to: spending on AI at a pace its earnings do not yet justify
finds.because: Spending guidance moved well above the original plan, setting a higher base for the 2026 figures that investors later judged.

finds.title: Alphabet Announces Third Quarter 2026 Results
finds.author: Alphabet Inc.
finds.source: U.S. Securities and Exchange Commission (Form 8-K, Exhibit 99.1, EDGAR)
finds.evidence_quote: Our AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries.
finds.line: Alphabet announced its third quarter 2026 results and said its AI investments are driving overall Search query growth, including commercial queries.
finds.about: Alphabet released these results on October 28, 2026, for the third quarter of that year. The company said its AI investments are driving overall Search query growth. It noted that this growth includes commercial queries.
finds.ties_to: a round of earnings that stoked fears
finds.because: This report put Alphabet's AI results and spending in front of investors, and the market's reaction followed within a day.

vetoed.line: The Johnson campaign aired the Daisy television ad against Barry Goldwater on September 7, 1964, during an NBC movie telecast.
